name: Just be famous theory

card.summary: The just-be-famous theory holds that fame, status and money can make a man attractive regardless of his face, so building a public profile is an alternative route to looking and being seen as attractive.
card.note: A forum framework; no study has tested it under this name.

quick.overview:
Just be famous (JBF) is a framework discussed on looksmaxxing forums. It argues that a man with average or below-average looks can still gain romantic and social success if he becomes famous, because celebrity brings attention and status that overshadow facial ratings.

It is usually raised in debates about how much looks matter, often with examples of publicly known couples where the man is rated lower on the community's scales. A looksmax.org thread uses the phrase in its title alongside a rating on the PSL scale and a supermodel partner.
quick.how: In practice the theory is a way of thinking rather than a routine: proponents point to building an audience, career or visibility as the lever instead of or alongside surgery and grooming.
quick.risks: The framework carries no physical risk. Critics inside and outside forums note that fame is rare and that attractiveness research shows halo effects in both directions.

lead: The just-be-famous theory (JBF) is a looksmaxxing-community claim that fame can substitute for conventional good looks in attracting partners and admiration. A looksmax.org thread titled with the phrase pairs it with a man rated 3.0 on the PSL scale who is dating a supermodel. [1]

The wiki's looks-focused framing places it as a counter-narrative: instead of changing the face, a person changes how the world perceives them. General reference material on celebrity notes that fame comes from broad public recognition and that celebrities are often perceived as having glowing or idealized qualities, a halo-like effect. [2]
No published study has tested the theory under this name. Researchers on celebrity and attraction discuss halo effects more broadly. [2]

chain: Looks weigh less in how others see you
angle.text: Proponents say visibility and status can raise how attractive a person is perceived to be, independent of facial features. It is used as an alternative or complement to cosmetic changes.

paras: Believers cite pairings of publicly known men rated modestly on forum scales with highly rated partners as illustrations. [1] The theory also appears in discussions about how much of attraction is facial structure versus social proof.

General sources describe fame as bringing a favorable public image and a tendency for the public to view celebrities as having above-average abilities. [2] No study cited here measures whether fame offsets facial attractiveness in dating outcomes.

lore.intro: The idea circulates on looksmax.org as a shorthand argument in debates about whether looks or status matter more. [1]

claims.claim: Fame can override a low facial rating
claims.believers: Proponents point to examples such as a 3.0 PSL man dating a supermodel. [1]
claims.experts: Reference material notes celebrity brings a favorable image and halo-like perceptions; no study tests the claim directly. [2]
